4.	In 1949, thousands of soldiers from Chiang Kai-shek’s defeated Kuomintang army fled south from Yunnan province into the jungles of a neighboring country with a weak central government. Cut off from their supply lines and their homeland now under Mao's control, these soldiers needed a way to fund themselves. They found it in a flower. The remote highland region where they settled had long been home to small-scale cultivation of the flower by indigenous hill tribes and it straddled three countries. The KMT soldiers industrialized the trade, directing farmers to expand cultivation and taxing their produce. During the Vietnam war, American soldiers established illicit trade channels, with this region providing up to 80% of the heroin reaching New York's streets. U.S. State Department official Marshall Green coined the two-word name X Y for this region in 1971. Today, the tourist village at its symbolic center has an _____ museum and a large golden Buddha.
